section_summary: This section (pages 321–400) consists primarily of official State Department and Treasury Department correspondence concerning reciprocal income tax exemptions under Section 116(h) of the Revenue Acts of 1936 and 1938 for Japanese government personnel stationed in the United States, including officials of the Imperial Japanese Navy, Army Ordnance, Government Railways, and Silk Intelligence Bureau. It also features a comprehensive 17-page official register of foreign agents registered with the Secretary of State under the Foreign Agents Registration Act of June 8, 1938. In addition, the section contains State Department memoranda and investigative field telegrams tracking the organization, branches, and representatives of the semi-private Japan Foreign Trade Federation (Boeki Kumiai Chuokai) in San Francisco, Seattle, and Houston.

subfiles.about: Concluding page of a State Department note confirming telegraphic notice to New York tax authorities regarding the tax-exempt compensation of Masatoki Nomura prior to his sailing.
subfiles.summary: This page contains the conclusion of a diplomatic note from the Department of State to the Japanese Ambassador. It confirms that internal revenue authorities in New York City were advised by telegraph in November regarding the exempt status of the official compensation received by Masatoki Nomura. Nomura, whose name had been included on the official roster, had scheduled his sailing from that port on November 26, 1937.
subfiles.title: Note from Department of State to Japanese Ambassador regarding Masatoki Nomura

subfiles.about: Confirms that eighteen Japanese officials attached to the Naval Inspector's Office in New York City are exempt from federal income taxation.
subfiles.from: Roswell Magill, Acting Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury Roswell Magill acknowledges the State Department's letter transmitting a note from the Japanese Ambassador dated November 20, 1937. Magill accepts the State Department's certification of reciprocity under the Revenue Act of 1936. The Treasury Department holds that the eighteen Japanese officials attached to the Naval Inspector's Office in New York City are exempt from federal income taxation on their official compensation, and internal revenue officials in New York City will be notified accordingly.
subfiles.title: Letter from Acting Secretary of the Treasury to Secretary of State regarding eighteen naval inspectors

subfiles.about: Informs the Japanese Ambassador that eighteen officials of the Naval Inspector's Office in New York City have been granted federal income tax exemption.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State refers to Japanese note No. 230 of November 20, 1937, which transmitted a roster of officials attached to the Naval Inspector's Office in New York City seeking tax exemption. The note communicates the Treasury Department's holding that, based on State Department certification, the eighteen officials named are exempt from federal income tax on salaries received from the Japanese Government for official services in the United States. Internal revenue officers have been instructed of this decision.
subfiles.title: Note from Secretary of State to Japanese Ambassador regarding eighteen naval inspection officials

subfiles.about: Transmits a list of fourteen naval officers and clerks attached to the Naval Inspector's Office in New York City requesting tax exemption.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador presents a list of fourteen officials attached to the Naval Inspector's Office of the Imperial Japanese Navy Department in New York requesting income tax exemption on their official salaries. The enclosed roster lists Engineer Captain Nobusuke Yamaguchi, six lieutenant commanders, two clerks, four assistant engineers, and a naval engineer. The Ambassador confirms that all individuals listed are of Japanese nationality and that their primary duty is inspecting materials purchased by the Japanese Government.
subfiles.title: Note No. 14 from Japanese Ambassador to Secretary of State transmitting roster of Naval Inspector's Office

subfiles.about: Certifies reciprocal tax exemption under Section 116(h) of the Revenue Act of 1936 for fourteen personnel of the Japanese Naval Inspector's Office in New York.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull transmits to Secretary of the Treasury Henry Morgenthau, Jr., a copy of Japanese note No. 14 containing the list of fourteen officials attached to the Naval Inspector's Office in New York. Hull certifies pursuant to Section 116(h) of the Revenue Act of 1936 that Japan grants equivalent tax exemptions to American government employees performing similar services in Japan. He requests that the Treasury Department grant the exemption and notify relevant internal revenue officers.
subfiles.title: Letter from Secretary of State to Secretary of the Treasury certifying tax exemption for Naval Inspector's Office personnel
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of note No. 14 requesting tax exemptions for Naval Inspector's Office personnel and advises that the matter has been referred to federal authorities.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges note No. 14 of February 4, 1938, from the Japanese Ambassador concerning tax exemption for personnel attached to the Naval Inspector's Office in New York City. The Japanese Ambassador is informed that copies of his note and enclosure have been submitted to the appropriate federal authorities. A further communication will be transmitted once a reply is received.
subfiles.title: Note from Secretary of State to Japanese Ambassador acknowledging note No. 14

subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of the State Department's certification concerning Naval Inspector's Office personnel and promises careful consideration.
subfiles.from: Roswell Magill, Acting Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury Roswell Magill acknowledges the State Department's letter of February 15, 1938, regarding tax exemption for officials attached to the Naval Inspector's Office of the Japanese Navy Department in New York City. Magill notes the State Department's recommendation that the officials be accorded tax-exempt status. He states that the matter will be given careful consideration by Treasury officials.
subfiles.title: Letter from Acting Secretary of the Treasury to Secretary of State acknowledging request for naval inspectors

subfiles.about: Cross-references a memorandum regarding an alleged $750,000 payment from Japanese sources to head a committee combating the anti-Japanese boycott.
subfiles.from: George S. Messersmith, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: This Document File Note cross-references a memorandum filed under decimal 611.9412/44 by Assistant Secretary of State George S. Messersmith. It records a conversation with E. A. Schachner, editor of China Today, concerning reports in the New York Times that Emil Rieve and Paolino Gerli had been appointed heads of a committee to combat the American boycott of Japanese goods. Schachner alleged that Gerli and his associates had received $750,000 from Japanese sources for this campaign.
subfiles.title: Document File Note regarding anti-boycott committee and Japanese funds

subfiles.about: Grants federal income tax exemption to fourteen officials of the Japanese Naval Inspector's Office in New York City.
subfiles.from: Roswell Magill, Acting Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury Roswell Magill replies to the State Department's letter of February 15, 1938, concerning fourteen officials of the Naval Inspector's Office in New York City. Acting on the State Department's certification under Section 116(h) of the Revenue Act of 1936, the Treasury Department rules that the officials are exempt from federal income taxation on official compensation received from the Japanese Government. The appropriate Collector of Internal Revenue will be instructed accordingly.
subfiles.title: Letter from Acting Secretary of the Treasury to Secretary of State granting tax exemption to naval inspectors

subfiles.about: Informs the Japanese Ambassador that fourteen officials of the Naval Inspector's Office in New York have been granted federal income tax exemption.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State refers to Japanese note No. 14 of February 4, 1938, requesting tax exemption for personnel of the Naval Inspector's Office in New York City. The Ambassador is advised that the Treasury Department, in view of State Department certification, has officially held the officials to be exempt from federal income taxation on compensation received from the Japanese Government. The Collector of Internal Revenue will be notified of their exempt status.
subfiles.title: Note from Secretary of State to Japanese Ambassador advising of tax exemption for naval inspectors

subfiles.about: Requests tax exemption for three officials attached to the Army Ordnance Inspector's Office of the Imperial Japanese War Department in New York.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador transmits a list of three officials attached to the Army Ordnance Inspector's Office of the Imperial Japanese War Department in New York seeking tax exemption on their official salaries. The enclosed roster names Lieutenant Colonel Torashiro Asano, Lieutenant Colonel Kooyu Moriya, and Assistant Engineer Hiroshi Matsuda. The note confirms that all three are Japanese nationals inspecting purchased materials, and notes that Matsuda expects to depart San Francisco for Japan on April 16, 1938.
subfiles.title: Note No. 41 from Japanese Ambassador to Secretary of State transmitting roster of Army Ordnance Inspector's Office

subfiles.about: Certifies reciprocal tax exemption under Section 116(h) for three Japanese Army Ordnance officials in New York, noting Matsuda's imminent departure.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull transmits the Japanese Ambassador's note No. 41 concerning Lieutenant Colonel Asano, Lieutenant Colonel Moriya, and Assistant Engineer Matsuda of the Army Ordnance Inspector's Office in New York. Hull certifies reciprocity under Section 116(h) of the Revenue Act of 1936, establishing that Japan extends equivalent exemptions to American personnel. He specifically points out that Matsuda expects to sail from San Francisco on April 16 and requests prompt notification to Treasury field offices.
subfiles.title: Letter from Secretary of State to Secretary of the Treasury certifying tax exemption for Army Ordnance officials
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of note No. 41 requesting tax exemptions for three Army Ordnance inspection officials.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges note No. 41 of March 29, 1938, from the Japanese Ambassador concerning income tax exemptions for Lieutenant Colonel Asano, Lieutenant Colonel Moriya, and Assistant Engineer Matsuda of the Army Ordnance Inspector's Office. The Japanese Ambassador is informed that the request has been submitted to federal authorities. A further communication will follow once a reply is received from the Treasury Department.
subfiles.title: Note from Secretary of State to Japanese Ambassador acknowledging note No. 41

subfiles.about: Confirms tax exemption for three Army Ordnance officials and orders notification of San Francisco tax agents for Matsuda's sailing.
subfiles.from: Roswell Magill, Acting Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury Roswell Magill acknowledges the State Department's letter of April 2, 1938, and rules that the three Japanese Army Ordnance officials in New York are exempt from federal income taxation. Noting that Hiroshi Matsuda expects to depart San Francisco for Japan on April 16, 1938, Magill states that the Collector of Internal Revenue and Internal Revenue Agent in Charge at San Francisco will be notified of his exempt status. The exemption applies to official compensation received from the Japanese Government.
subfiles.title: Letter from Acting Secretary of the Treasury to Secretary of State granting tax exemption to Army Ordnance personnel

subfiles.about: Informs the Japanese Ambassador of the tax-exempt ruling for Army Ordnance personnel and clearance instructions sent to San Francisco for Matsuda.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State refers to Japanese note No. 41 and informs the Japanese Ambassador that the Treasury Department has granted federal income tax exemption to Lieutenant Colonel Asano, Lieutenant Colonel Moriya, and Assistant Engineer Matsuda. The note adds that the Collector of Internal Revenue and Internal Revenue Agent in Charge at San Francisco were notified regarding the exempt status of Matsuda's compensation prior to his sailing on April 16, 1938. Official salaries received from the Japanese Government are confirmed as exempt.
subfiles.title: Note from Secretary of State to Japanese Ambassador advising of tax exemption for Army Ordnance personnel

subfiles.about: Requests tax exemption for Kenjiro Nishimura of the Silk Intelligence Bureau prior to his departure for Europe on the S.S. Bremen.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador informs the Secretary of State that Kenjiro Nishimura, a clerk of the Japanese Department of Agriculture and Forestry, requests exemption from taxation on his official salary. The Ambassador notes that Nishimura has lived in the United States since January 1935 as a clerk of the Japanese Government Silk Intelligence Bureau in New York. The note requests expedited handling as Nishimura plans to leave New York for Europe on May 28, 1938, aboard the S.S. Bremen.
subfiles.title: Note No. 86 from Japanese Ambassador to Secretary of State requesting tax exemption for Kenjiro Nishimura

subfiles.about: Certifies reciprocal tax exemption under Section 116(h) for Kenjiro Nishimura of the Japanese Government Silk Intelligence Bureau.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull transmits a copy of Japanese note No. 86 concerning Kenjiro Nishimura to Secretary of the Treasury Henry Morgenthau, Jr. Hull certifies pursuant to Section 116(h) of the Revenue Act of 1936 that Japan grants equivalent exemptions to American personnel. He calls attention to Nishimura's planned departure from New York on May 28 aboard the S.S. Bremen and requests that Treasury advise the State Department promptly for communication to the Japanese Ambassador.
subfiles.title: Letter from Secretary of State to Secretary of the Treasury certifying tax exemption for Kenjiro Nishimura
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of note No. 86 and states that tax authorities have been alerted to Nishimura's departure date.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges the Japanese Ambassador's note No. 86 of May 21, 1938, regarding the desired income tax exemption for Kenjiro Nishimura of the Japanese Department of Agriculture and Forestry. The Japanese Ambassador is informed that a copy was transmitted to the appropriate federal authority with attention invited to Nishimura's plan to sail for Europe on May 28 on the S.S. Bremen. A further communication will follow upon receipt of a reply.
subfiles.title: Note from Secretary of State to Japanese Ambassador acknowledging note No. 86 regarding Kenjiro Nishimura

subfiles.about: Cross-references a Japanese Embassy note requesting an income tax refund for Yukio Suetsugu of the Silk Intelligence Bureau.
subfiles.summary: This Document File Note cross-references a note from the Japanese Embassy dated June 11, 1938, filed under decimal 811.5123/2568. The referenced communication relates to the payment of income tax by Yukio Suetsugu, Technical Expert of the Japanese Government Silk Intelligence Bureau in New York City. The Embassy requested a refund of income taxes paid by Suetsugu based on his official governmental status.
subfiles.title: Document File Note regarding tax refund request for Yukio Suetsugu

subfiles.about: Confirms tax exemption for Kenjiro Nishimura and reports prior notification sent to the New York Customhouse.
subfiles.from: Stephen B. Gibbons, Acting Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury Stephen B. Gibbons responds to the State Department's letter of May 24, 1938, concerning Kenjiro Nishimura. Based on State Department certification under Section 116(h) of the Revenue Act of 1936, the Treasury Department rules that Nishimura is exempt from federal income taxation on official compensation received from the Japanese Government. Gibbons adds that the Collector of Internal Revenue at the New York Customhouse was advised of Nishimura's exempt status on May 25, 1938.
subfiles.title: Letter from Acting Secretary of the Treasury to Secretary of State granting tax exemption to Kenjiro Nishimura

subfiles.about: Informs the Japanese Ambassador that Kenjiro Nishimura was granted tax exemption and that New York tax officials were duly notified.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State refers to Japanese note No. 86 and the Department's reply of May 24 concerning Kenjiro Nishimura of the Japanese Department of Agriculture and Forestry. The Japanese Ambassador is informed that the Treasury Department has held Nishimura exempt from federal income taxation on compensation received from the Japanese Government. The note confirms that under date of May 25, 1938, the Collector of Internal Revenue at the New York Customhouse was formally advised of his exempt status.
subfiles.title: Note from Secretary of State to Japanese Ambassador advising of tax exemption for Kenjiro Nishimura

subfiles.about: Requests tax exemption for four officials attached to the Imperial Japanese Government Railway Office in New York.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador submits a list of four officials attached to the Imperial Japanese Government Railway Office in New York City, requesting exemption from taxation on their official salaries. The enclosed roster names Civil Engineer Yasumitsu Okazaki, Secretaries Fuwazo Tanaka and Tsutoo Takase, and Clerk Tatsuichi Nakai. The Ambassador affirms that all four officials are Japanese nationals whose principal duty is inspecting materials purchased by the Japanese Government.
subfiles.title: Note No. 184 from Japanese Ambassador to Secretary of State transmitting roster of Government Railway Office

subfiles.about: Requests the addition of Engineer Captain Todomu Nakamura and Naval Engineer Moritoshi Maeda to the tax-exempt naval roster in New York.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador requests that two incoming naval officers be added to the list of officials attached to the Naval Inspector's Office in New York seeking tax exemption. Engineer Captain Todomu Nakamura took charge of the office at 1 Madison Avenue on October 20, 1938, succeeding Engineer Captain Nobusuke Yamaguchi for a two-year tour. Naval Engineer Moritoshi Maeda was scheduled to leave Japan on October 24 aboard the Chichibu Maru for an eighteen-month assignment inspecting materials.
subfiles.title: Note No. 191 from Japanese Ambassador to Secretary of State requesting addition of naval officers to tax-exempt roster

subfiles.about: Confirms federal income tax exemption under the Revenue Act of 1938 for four Japanese Government Railway officials in New York.
subfiles.from: John W. Hanes, Acting Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury John W. Hanes responds to the State Department's letter of November 8, 1938, concerning Japanese Government Railway officials Okazaki, Tanaka, Takase, and Nakai. Hanes acknowledges the State Department's certification under Section 116(h) of the Revenue Act of 1938 regarding reciprocal tax treatment in Japan. The Treasury Department holds that their official salaries are exempt from federal income tax, and interested officers of the Department will be notified accordingly.
subfiles.title: Letter from Acting Secretary of the Treasury to Secretary of State granting tax exemption to railway officials

subfiles.about: Transmits a Treasury Department excerpt confirming tax exemption for four Japanese Government Railway officials in New York.
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of State refers to Japanese note No. 184 of October 12, 1938, concerning tax exemption for personnel of the Imperial Japanese Government Railway Office in New York City. An excerpt from the Treasury Department's letter of December 2, 1938, is enclosed, showing that the requested income tax exemption has been granted. The ruling exempts compensation received from the Japanese Government for official services in the United States.
subfiles.title: Note from Acting Secretary of State to Japanese Ambassador advising of tax exemption for railway officials

subfiles.about: Requests tax exemption for Mechanical Engineer Tatsuo Shiraki of the Japanese Government Railways succeeding K. Yamanouchi.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador notifies the Acting Secretary of State of the appointment of Tatsuo Shiraki, Mechanical Engineer, as a resident representative of the Japanese Government Railways in New York. Shiraki succeeds K. Yamanouchi, who left New York for Europe aboard the S.S. Queen Mary on September 21, 1938. The Ambassador requests that Shiraki, a Japanese national, be added to the list of railway officials exempt from taxation on their official compensation.
subfiles.title: Note No. 216 from Japanese Ambassador to Acting Secretary of State requesting tax exemption for Tatsuo Shiraki

subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of note No. 216 concerning Tatsuo Shiraki and states the request was referred to federal authorities.
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Japanese note No. 216 of December 8, 1938, concerning tax exemption for Tatsuo Shiraki of the Japanese Government Railways in New York. The note references Shiraki's succession to K. Yamanouchi, who departed from the United States. The Ambassador is informed that a copy of his note has been transmitted to competent federal authorities for appropriate action.
subfiles.title: Note from Acting Secretary of State to Japanese Ambassador acknowledging note No. 216

subfiles.about: Certifies reciprocal tax exemption under Section 116(h) of the Revenue Act of 1938 for Tatsuo Shiraki of the Japanese Government Railways.
subfiles.from: Sumner Welles, Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of State Sumner Welles transmits Japanese note No. 216 concerning Tatsuo Shiraki, successor to K. Yamanouchi at the Japanese Government Railways New York office. Welles refers to the Department's circular note of August 15, 1938, aimed at preventing tax difficulties for departing foreign employees. Welles certifies reciprocity under Section 116(h) of the Revenue Act of 1938 and requests that Treasury officials be advised so Shiraki may be exempted from income taxes.
subfiles.title: Letter from Acting Secretary of State to Secretary of the Treasury certifying tax exemption for Tatsuo Shiraki
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: Requests tax exemption for Commander Tadashi Mikami, Lieutenant Commander Kiyomi Watanabe, and Naval Engineer Toshiyuki Mori in New York.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador requests tax exemption for three incoming naval officers attached to the Naval Inspector's Office in New York. Commander Tadashi Mikami was scheduled to arrive in Seattle on December 31 aboard the Hikawa Maru for a two-year tour. Engineer Lieutenant Commander Kiyomi Watanabe and Naval Engineer Toshiyuki Mori arrived at San Francisco on December 22 aboard the Chichibu Maru; all are Japanese nationals whose duties involve inspecting purchased materials.
subfiles.title: Note No. 240 from Japanese Ambassador to Acting Secretary of State transmitting roster of arriving naval officers

subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of note No. 240 requesting tax exemption for three arriving naval officers.
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of State acknowledges note No. 240 of December 28, 1938, requesting that three incoming Japanese naval officers be added to the tax-exempt list for the Naval Inspector's Office in New York City. The Japanese Ambassador is informed that copies of his note and enclosure have been forwarded to the competent authority of the United States Government for appropriate action.
subfiles.title: Note from Acting Secretary of State to Japanese Ambassador acknowledging note No. 240

subfiles.about: Certifies reciprocal tax exemption under Section 116(h) of the Revenue Act of 1938 for naval officers Mikami, Watanabe, and Mori.
subfiles.from: Sumner Welles, Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of State Sumner Welles transmits Japanese note No. 240 listing Commander Tadashi Mikami, Lieutenant Commander Kiyomi Watanabe, and Naval Engineer Toshiyuki Mori. Welles certifies under Section 116(h) of the Revenue Act of 1938 that Japan grants equivalent exemptions to American personnel in Japan. He requests that Treasury authorities notify internal revenue collectors so the three officers may receive exemption on their official salaries.
subfiles.title: Letter from Acting Secretary of State to Secretary of the Treasury certifying tax exemption for three naval officers
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: Acknowledges the State Department's certification for Tatsuo Shiraki and states the matter is receiving careful consideration.
subfiles.from: Wayne C. Taylor, Acting Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury Wayne C. Taylor acknowledges the State Department's letter of December 22, 1938, enclosing the Japanese Ambassador's request on behalf of Tatsuo Shiraki. Taylor states that the question of granting federal income tax exemption on Shiraki's official compensation is receiving the careful consideration of the Treasury Department. The State Department will be advised of the determination at the earliest practicable date.
subfiles.title: Letter from Acting Secretary of the Treasury to Secretary of State regarding Tatsuo Shiraki

subfiles.about: Requests sailing tax clearance for Minoru Yagami of the Japanese Government Railways departing aboard the Aquitania.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador refers to the State Department's circular note of August 15, 1938, concerning departure tax procedures. He states that Minoru Yagami, Secretary of the Japanese Government Railways in New York, will depart for Japan on February 4, 1939, aboard the S.S. Aquitania. The Ambassador requests necessary administrative steps so that Yagami, whose income derived solely from official Japanese Government compensation, may depart without difficulties regarding income taxes.
subfiles.title: Note No. 8 from Japanese Ambassador to Secretary of State regarding tax clearance for Minoru Yagami

subfiles.about: Acknowledges note No. 8 and confirms referral to federal authorities for Minoru Yagami's departure tax clearance.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges note No. 8 of January 14, 1939, regarding Minoru Yagami's scheduled departure from New York on February 4 aboard the S.S. Aquitania. The note states that a copy was transmitted to the competent authority of the United States Government to ensure Yagami's exemption from income tax on official compensation. This step is intended to allow his departure without administrative complications.
subfiles.title: Note from Secretary of State to Japanese Ambassador acknowledging note No. 8 regarding Minoru Yagami

subfiles.about: Certifies reciprocal tax exemption under Section 116(h) of the Revenue Act of 1938 for Minoru Yagami prior to his departure from New York.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull transmits the Japanese Embassy's note No. 8 concerning Minoru Yagami, Secretary of the Japanese Government Railways in New York. Hull certifies reciprocity under Section 116(h) of the Revenue Act of 1938, establishing that Japan extends equivalent exemptions to American personnel. Noting Yagami's scheduled departure on February 4 aboard the S.S. Aquitania, Hull requests prompt notification to Treasury field officers.
subfiles.title: Letter from Secretary of State to Secretary of the Treasury certifying tax exemption for Minoru Yagami
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of the supplemental list of Japanese naval officers and states the request is under consideration.
subfiles.from: John W. Hanes, Acting Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury John W. Hanes acknowledges the State Department's letter of January 6, 1939, transmitting Despatch No. 240 from the Japanese Ambassador. Hanes notes the supplemental list of Japanese Government employees seeking federal income tax exemption on their official compensation. He states that the matter is receiving careful consideration and further advice will be provided at the earliest practicable date.
subfiles.title: Letter from Acting Secretary of the Treasury to Secretary of State acknowledging naval list

subfiles.about: Records Canadian inquiry concerning the Central Bureau of Trade Associations of Japan and its status in the United States.
subfiles.from: Joseph W. Ballantine and Maxwell M. Hamilton
keywords: Central Bureau of Trade Associations of Japan
subfiles.summary: Dr. Walter A. Riddell, Counselor of the Canadian Legation, informs State Department officers Hamilton and Ballantine of a Japanese proposal to establish a branch of the Central Bureau of Trade Associations of Japan at Winnipeg to promote trade and resolve disputes. Riddell inquires whether the organization operates in the United States or if a similar approach was made to Washington. Hamilton replies that no approach was made and notes that entities like the South Manchuria Railway Company maintain offices in New York without requiring official government permission.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation between Canadian Counselor Riddell and State Department officials Ballantine and Hamilton

subfiles.about: Identifies the Central Bureau of Trade Associations of Japan as the Japan Foreign Trade Federation headed by Kenji Kodama.
keywords: Japanese Committee on Trade and Information
subfiles.summary: FE officer Schuler reports that trade publications identify the Central Bureau of Trade Associations of Japan (Boeki Kumiai Chuokai) as the Japan Foreign Trade Federation, headed by Kenji Kodama. Formed on July 1, 1938, the federation represents thousands of merchants and maintains trade agencies abroad, including San Francisco, and correspondents in Seattle, Chicago, and Houston. Schuler suggests investigating whether it connects to the Japanese Committee on Trade and Information in San Francisco and recommending foreign agent registration inquiries.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from FE (Schuler) to Hamilton regarding Japan Foreign Trade Federation
subfiles.to: Maxwell M. Hamilton, Chief, Division of Far Eastern Affairs

subfiles.about: Official roster of 236 agents of foreign principals registered in the United States pursuant to the Foreign Agents Registration Act of June 8, 1938.
subfiles.summary: This 17-page official register lists registration numbers 1 through 236 under the Foreign Agents Registration Act of June 8, 1938. Each entry provides the registrant's name and business address across various cities in the United States, Puerto Rico, Canada, and Cuba. Registrants include foreign government travel bureaus, news agencies, publicity firms, steamship lines, trade chambers, and individual public relations representatives and legal counsel representing foreign principals.
subfiles.title: List of Agents of Foreign Principals Registered with the Secretary of State under the Act of June 8, 1938

subfiles.about: Reports that Nobuzo Kawai in Houston is the correspondent for the Japan Foreign Trade Federation.
subfiles.summary: Post Office Inspector Gagne wires Chief Special Agent R. C. Bannerman from Houston, Texas, regarding Japanese trade personnel. He confirms that Nobuzo Kawai, residing at 413 West Clay Street in Houston, has been the local correspondent for the Japan Foreign Trade Federation for about one month. Kawai previously served as a representative of the Japanese Ministry of Commerce and Industry.
subfiles.title: Telegram from Post Office Inspector Gagne to Bannerman regarding Nobuzo Kawai
subfiles.to: R. C. Bannerman, Chief Special Agent, Department of State

subfiles.about: Reports investigative findings on Tadao Yasuda and Japanese trade representation in Seattle.
subfiles.summary: Special Agent Caine reports from Seattle that the Japan Foreign Trade Federation is not registered locally, but Tadao Yasuda succeeded Masao Matsumoto on October 1 as agent of the Ministry of Commerce and Industry. Yasuda, a 35-year-old former commissioner who arrived on the Hikawa Maru on September 21 with his family, works as a clerk in the Japanese Consulate's commerce department. He rents Post Office Box 22 at Nippon Station and maintains an office and residence linked to the consulate.
subfiles.title: Telegram from Special Agent Caine to Bannerman regarding Tadao Yasuda in Seattle
subfiles.to: R. C. Bannerman, Chief Special Agent, Department of State

subfiles.about: Confirms that H. K. Watanabe's Nippon Trade Agency in San Francisco is the local branch of the Japan Foreign Trade Federation.
subfiles.summary: Acting Special Agent Hugdal cables Chief Special Agent R. C. Bannerman from San Francisco regarding the Japan Foreign Trade Federation. He verifies that the Nippon Trade Agency at 549 Market Street, managed by H. K. Watanabe, serves as the local branch of the federation. He adds that Kenji Kodama, referenced in previous State Department inquiries, is currently in Tokyo.
subfiles.title: Telegram from Acting Special Agent Hugdal to Bannerman regarding Nippon Trade Agency in San Francisco
subfiles.to: R. C. Bannerman, Chief Special Agent, Department of State

subfiles.about: Summarizes investigative findings on Japan Foreign Trade Federation representatives in San Francisco, Houston, and Seattle.
subfiles.summary: Schuler notes that FE's December 12 findings regarding the Japan Foreign Trade Federation were communicated by telephone to Dr. Riddell of the Canadian Legation. Supplemental intelligence confirmed that H. K. Watanabe in San Francisco, Nobuzo Kawai in Houston, and Tadao Yasuda in Seattle represent the federation and the Ministry of Commerce and Industry. It is recommended that this information be transmitted to the Division of Controls (CA) to send foreign agent registration circulars to the individuals in Houston and Seattle.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by Schuler regarding Japan Foreign Trade Federation representatives
